prompt: what was the Earth's climate like during the earliest Cambrian period
judge_reasoning: Candidate 1 gives a largely consistent, high-level picture (warm greenhouse conditions, ice-free poles, higher CO2/sea levels, indirect inference) without introducing clear, major timeline errors. Candidate 2 is less reliable because it ties the end of the Marinoan glaciation to the earliest Cambrian, which is off by roughly tens of millions of years. Candidate 3 and especially Candidate 4 include more highly specific, likely-unverifiable climatic and biogeochemical numbers; Candidate 4 also claims earliest Cambrian “first” land plants/mosses, which conflicts with the generally accepted appearance of land plants later (Silurian/Ordovician). Overall, Candidate 1 is the most credible and best aligned answer to the prompt.
